title: Product Development Intelligence Suite
description: A concise guide to choosing a tool, understanding the architecture, interpreting what each tool reports, and working with portable results.

sections.title: Overview
sections.intro: PDIS turns product-development documents into traceable analysis while keeping document quality, document alignment, and external evidence as separate responsibilities. Each tool is told apart by the authority it judges against, and a tool that judges nothing only reports what a source already states.

items.title: Choose a tool
items.text: Start with the question you need answered rather than a generic analysis.

items.title: Provide context
items.text: Upload the source material and select the requested product context.

items.title: Inspect the trace
items.text: Review cited blocks, sources, exclusions, and limitations before downloading the result.

content.title: Why this matters
content.text: Inspector, Aligner, Screener, and Scout intentionally produce different outputs, because each judges against a different authority. None is a funding recommendation or a universal product score.

sections.title: Tools
sections.intro: Tools are grouped by audience and role. Availability belongs to the individual tool, while external provider links appear only where they are required.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.intro: PDIS keeps document parsing, analysis, API composition, and presentation behind explicit contracts so each layer can change without silently changing system meaning.

items.description: Collects configuration and files, carries review state, and renders current results. It does not hold provider credentials.
Validates requests, injects provider and connector clients, and streams service progress or final responses.
Run stateless Inspector, Aligner, Screener, Scout, Chunker, Searcher, and Assistant workflows through typed contracts.
Owns provider clients, controlled vocabularies, and public product documentation used across services and the web application.
Ordered text, table, and retained image blocks carry stable IDs so every claim can point back to source material.
The client carries drafts and results; services do not create hidden workspace sessions.
Final Inspector, Aligner, Screener, and Scout artifacts package analysis separately from their parsed source documents.
Models perform bounded semantic judgments; schemas and deterministic calculations enforce structural contracts and reproducible arithmetic.

sections.title: Scout evidence
sections.intro: Scout reads what your document commits to, searches outside evidence for it, and keeps four judgments separate so none of them becomes a score.

items.description: Current evidence for the document-bound field or claim.
LMIC, implementation, access, regulatory, and local-language evidence.
Evidence that may weaken or constrain the stated target.
Comparable products or programs that show whether an approach has been tried.
What one piece of outside evidence does to the target this document states: Conflicts, Supports, Adds context, or Unrelated. One relation per insight.
How well justified the target is: Well grounded, Partly grounded, Thinly grounded, Unsupported, or Grounding unknown.
The numbers this document states that external measurements can be compared against. Read only from passages a resolved target cites.

How directly prior work matches: Direct precedent, Adjacent precedent, No precedent found, or Precedent unknown. The outcome is reported separately, and is a different question: Favorable outcome, Mixed outcome, Unfavorable outcome, or Outcome unknown.

How close a retrieved record's subject is to your product: Direct, Analogous, Adjacent, Unrelated, or Unknown. It asks what a record is about, where Relation to document target asks what a piece of evidence does to a claim. The two share the word Unrelated and mean different things by it, and a record can be Analogous on this axis while its insight is Unrelated on that one. Adjacent here also means something different from Adjacent precedent, which is about how directly prior work matches.
The pre-retrieval checkpoint for deciding whether a document-owned quantitative proposal is a real measurable commitment rather than background, an example, or a rejected alternative.
The exact cited document text from which a proposal was mapped.
One number pulled out of the document for review, before anyone has accepted it. Accepted ones become the measurable targets on the result.

The fields one document number applies to. Defines means it sets the field, constrains means it limits it, and context for means it stays traceable without driving any search or statistic. These are readings of one number, not records that update together.
Measure, endpoint, intervention, population, regimen, time horizon, statistic, and conditions describe what the target or measurement means.
Exact requires an axis to match; compatible permits variation within its stated scope; unconstrained does not restrict that axis; unknown requires review rather than an inferred rule.
A review recommendation only. It is not a completed human decision and does not admit a target or measurement.
The proposal or comparison could not be recommended confidently and remains explicit rather than being silently admitted.
A number Scout kept for audit but could not pin to a single value it could verify, so it stays out of retrieval and statistics.
The post-retrieval checkpoint for deciding whether a cited numeric result is comparable enough to enter descriptive statistics for one document target.
The target and one measurement shown side by side. Whether they match is the model's reading; admitting the measurement is the reviewer's decision.
Alternative estimates from one evidence unit remain auditable, but at most one may contribute so one source population is not counted repeatedly.

The measurements that entered the statistics: each quoted from its source, measuring the same quantity, and counted once per source. A number is only taken from published literature, a trial registry or a regulator.

content.title: Quantitative review
content.text: Two model providers do the two steps, so neither checks its own work. Anthropic reads the document's numbers and the retrieved measurements into a comparable shape. OpenAI then recommends, separately, whether each one should be admitted, excluded, or looked at by a person. A person decides admission. Code checks the rest: provenance, units, duplicates, and arithmetic.

content.title: Calibration is descriptive
content.text: Quantitative distributions describe only the admitted comparator cohort. They are not confidence intervals, population estimates, causal claims, or probabilities of success.

sections.title: Assistant context
sections.intro: Assistant is a stateless, read-only navigator over the context available in the current browser workspace.

items.description: Assistant can find and read these curated process, architecture, and interpretation sections on demand.
Assistant receives current tool names, responsibilities, audiences, availability, and external-provider labels.

Declared procedures Assistant can follow: reading two results together, or turning one into a list of requests or a passage safe to quote. Each names the results it needs and is offered only when the workspace holds them; one that cannot run is still listed, with the run that is missing. A skill is not a pipeline. It runs nothing and reads only results a tool's pipeline already produced.
Assistant can navigate eligible current analyses and direct utility outputs submitted by the client.
Assistant can find and read the exact parsed text and retained image blocks packaged with available results.
Files added in chat become temporary parsed context for that conversation; they do not become analysis evidence.
Assistant may open a URL only when it already appears in a submitted result. It never starts a new evidence search.

content.title: Context is selected on demand
content.text: Assistant starts from compact maps and uses bounded tools to read only the relevant documentation section, result subtree, document blocks, or cited source. It does not place every available artifact into every model prompt.

content.title: One workspace lifecycle
content.text: Conversation text, loaded results, source blocks, and attachments remain together in the current in-memory browser workspace and reset together on reload. Final results become durable only through explicit export and import.

content.title: Workspace boundary
content.text: Assistant cannot inspect an active review draft, mutate a result, run a tool workflow, or retrieve uncited evidence. An absent result means that no eligible current final result was submitted.

content.title: A skill composes results; it does not judge them
content.text: Each tool judges against one authority and never reads another tool's output, which is what stops two of them contradicting each other. A skill is a reader: it holds finished results, states which finding on each side a claim rests on, and issues no verdict of its own. So it can say that a candidate falls short of a target the evidence disputes, something neither result says alone, without either result changing.

sections.title: Saved results
sections.intro: Every tool that produces a result (Inspector, Aligner, Screener, and Scout) downloads a portable, versioned artifact. Their analysis and source documents travel together.

items.description: Tool-specific judgments, traces, and derived views.
Ordered text, table, and retained image blocks with stable IDs.
Read-only navigation across current client-held results, blocks, visuals, and already-cited URLs.

content.title: Current contract only
content.text: Imports accept only final artifacts produced by the current application version. Source spans, visuals, query lineage, and retrieval provenance must already be complete.

sections.title: Development
sections.intro: Repository setup, environment variables, deployment, contribution guidance, and service contracts live with the code so they remain versioned with the implementation.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.intro: Answers to the questions that change how a result should be read, or how it should not be quoted.

items.question: Does any of this tell me whether to fund something?
items.answer: No. Each tool answers one narrow question against one authority: a template, another document, a gate's question bank, or published evidence. None of them produces a recommendation, a readiness verdict, or a product score. The judgement stays with the reader.

items.question: Can I get one number for how a document did?
items.answer: No, and there deliberately is none. Every result is several states that sum to a total, and one figure blending “the document says it”, “it says half of it” and “nobody has asked yet” would be a number no tool computed. Quote the largest state with its denominator instead.

items.question: I ran the same document twice and the findings are not identical. Is something wrong?
items.answer: No, and it is worth knowing which half moved. Identical on every run: which questions are asked, the denominator they are counted against, which blocks a finding is allowed to cite, and what is excluded and why. Those are fixed by the rubric, the question bank, and deterministic checks, not by the model. What varies: which findings surface first, how each is worded, and, for Scout, which sources a search happens to reach. So a second run may order or phrase things differently while the ledger it was judged against is unchanged. Read a difference as a difference in emphasis, not as a change in what the document contains. If you need the two side by side, see “Can I compare two runs?”.

items.question: Can I compare two runs?
items.answer: Only where the authority is fixed. Inspector and Screener compare line by line, because the same rubric and the same question bank are asked every time. Aligner does not: its requirements are read out of the reference document, so two runs may find a different number of them and neither total is a baseline. Scout compares only within the same published-since window.

items.question: What happens if I choose the wrong document type?
items.answer: You get a confident result about the wrong thing. The type decides how the file is parsed and which rubric or configuration it is read against, and nothing checks that the file matches the type you chose.

items.question: Why can I attach a PDF as context but not upload one for review?
items.answer: Because the two are read differently. An uploaded document becomes citable blocks, and every citation depends on structure being read from the file, which a PDF does not declare, so a table rebuilt from where glyphs landed can merge unrelated columns and still look correct. Context is read once into a prompt: never chunked, never cited, never checked against a quote. So a format that declares no structure loses nothing there, and an answer from it says so by naming its source instead of a passage.

items.question: What does “not found” actually mean?
items.answer: That the question was read against everything you supplied and nothing addressed it. It is not a claim that one of your documents should have contained it: many of these questions ask about operational facts or matters of judgement that no profile or plan would ever carry, and the tool cannot tell those apart from a real omission. What it can tell you is which discipline owns the question.

items.question: Why does a requirement say the candidate falls short when the profile is the unrealistic one?
items.answer: Because a comparison runs one way: it reports whether the measured document meets the bar, and never whether the bar is reasonable. Whether a target is achievable is Scout's question, run separately, and the assistant can read both results together.

items.question: Can I compare two versions of the same document?
items.answer: Not today. A comparison is declared between two different document types, and two revisions of one type are refused, because “what changed between drafts” is a different question from “does this meet the bar”.

items.question: Does it search the internet on its own?
items.answer: Only Scout retrieves anything, only from the sources its configuration enables, and it reads your document first, and every query is bound to a passage in it. Ask never starts a search and may open a URL only when a result already cites it.

items.question: Where does my document go?
items.answer: It is parsed in the service, and its text and images travel to the model provider inside each request. Nothing is kept on a server: the workspace lives in your browser and resets on reload, so the only durable copy is a result you export. A file attached as context is read into text once, used for that run, and discarded. It is never stored and never becomes part of a result.

items.question: Why is a chart or tab absent?
items.answer: Derived views appear only when their required data exists. An absent chart does not imply a favorable or unfavorable result.

items.question: Can I import an older result?
items.answer: No. Imports accept only final results produced by the current application contract, and the message names which version failed so you know whether to re-run one tool or all of them.

items.question: Can Ask see a review I have not finished?
items.answer: No. It receives final results, direct utility outputs, their source blocks, and conversation attachments. An active review draft stays in your browser, and an absent result is reported as absent rather than guessed at from other context.

sections.title: Pipelines
sections.intro: Explore how each PDIS tool moves from source material to a traceable result, then expand load-bearing stages for their technical flow. A pipeline is what a run executes, stage by stage, and every one below is one. Assistant's pipeline is here too, and the skills it can follow are one step inside it: a skill reads finished results and runs no pipeline of its own.

content.title: Interactive architecture
content.description: Choose a tool for its end-to-end flow. Select a stage to inspect what it consumes, produces, and guarantees; stages with a technical flow can expand in place.

graphs.title: Inspector
graphs.summary: Turns one parsed development document and its authored rubric into one verdict per rubric unit, each citing the passage it was read from, plus cited cross-section conflicts.

nodes.title: Document and rubric
nodes.summary: One parsed document enters with its configured rubric.

nodes.title: Section mapping
nodes.summary: Every source block is assigned once to the configured section taxonomy.

nodes.title: Unit assessment
nodes.summary: One bounded call per rubric unit asks how it stands, in one word from one closed vocabulary. One question, one answer: a unit carries exactly one verdict.
outputs: One verdict per unit, with exact block lineage

nodes.title: Assembly and consistency
nodes.summary: Code joins the rubric with the verdicts and orders them, while a separate model pass finds cited cross-section conflicts.
outputs: Section counts, summed from the units

nodes.title: Portable inspection
nodes.summary: The final analysis and parsed source document travel together.

graphs.title: Aligner
graphs.summary: Reads what one document requires and checks another against it, one requirement at a time. A comparison runs one way: the reference document sets the bar.

nodes.title: Document set
nodes.summary: Two or more documents enter, each named by its type, with shared product context.
nodes.guarantee: No stage knows how many documents a run holds; the count is whatever was supplied.

nodes.title: Comparison resolution
nodes.summary: Configuration declares which ordered pairs of document types compare; a run resolves those whose documents are both present.
outputs: Resolved comparisons, each with the question it asks
nodes.guarantee: A set of documents that forms no declared comparison fails before parsing rather than returning an empty result.

nodes.title: Parallel parse
nodes.summary: Each document is parsed through its own chunker configuration, resolved from its type.
inputs: A chunker configuration per document type
nodes.guarantee: Every block keeps the identity of the document it came from.

nodes.title: Requirement extraction
nodes.summary: One call per comparison reads the reference document and lists every requirement it states, each cited to the passage that states it.
outputs: Atomic requirements, each with its citation
nodes.guarantee: A requirement is a quotation of a demand, never a judgement about it. Compound sentences are split, because one verdict cannot cover three separate facts.

nodes.title: Requirement verdicts
nodes.summary: One bounded call per requirement, each reading the document being measured: meets, exceeds, falls short, not comparable, or not addressed.
outputs: A one-way verdict, with the passages behind it
What is still to close, where the verdict has a gap
nodes.guarantee: The schema offers only the measured document's blocks, so a verdict cannot be justified by citing the document that set the bar.

nodes.title: Portable result
nodes.summary: Every requirement, its verdict, and the passages on both sides form one downloadable result.
nodes.guarantee: Every verdict is navigable to the passage it was read from, and every requirement to the passage that sets it.

graphs.title: Scout
graphs.summary: Binds document authority before retrieval, preserves source-lane lineage, and reports orthogonal evidence signals without a blended score.

nodes.title: Parsed document
nodes.summary: Ordered blocks and selected product context establish the source boundary.
inputs: Organization, document type, intervention, and indication
outputs: The evidence window every later statistic describes

nodes.title: Canonical claim authority
nodes.summary: Fields, claims, atomic targets, entities, and exact spans converge before search.
nodes.details: Fixed TPP fields and extracted IPDP claims converge to one Attribute contract; quantitative targets remain in one document-owned ledger.
nodes.guarantee: Downstream stages consume this meaning and cannot rewrite it.

children.title: Indication check
children.summary: Stops only a clear, block-cited mismatch; ambiguity remains explicit.

children.title: Field and claim binding
children.summary: Resolves each canonical field or dynamic claim to exact document spans.

children.title: Atomic target mapping
children.summary: Splits owned spans into measurable targets with semantic profiles and comparator policies.

children.title: Document-wide reconciliation
children.summary: Groups calculation-compatible representations without rewriting claim meaning.

nodes.title: Target review
nodes.summary: AI recommendations and explicit decisions determine which proposals drive retrieval.
nodes.guarantee: Contextual links remain traceable but never create statistics.

nodes.title: Intent and source fan-out
nodes.summary: Neutral query intents are compiled and executed by independent source adapters.
outputs: Findings with intent, target, adapter, connector, query, and URL lineage
nodes.guarantee: Source failures remain isolated and source grammar never leaks into Scout.

children.title: Source-neutral intents
children.summary: General, geographic, counterfactual, precedent, and adjacent tracks add coverage without overwriting each other.

children.title: Adapter planning
children.summary: Each adapter applies its source grammar, applicability rules, rate limit, and request budget.

children.title: Bounded execution
children.summary: Runnable source lanes execute concurrently without slow lanes consuming all capacity.

children.title: Finding normalization
children.summary: Adapters return one finding contract while preserving every retrieval path.

children.title: Publication window
children.summary: A requested window is applied where evidence enters the run, not at display, so every later statistic describes the cohort it admitted. Findings their source left undated stay admitted, and each trace names the URLs the window held out.

nodes.title: Independent evidence axes
nodes.summary: Insights feed target relation, grounding, precedent, and quantitative calibration separately.
nodes.guarantee: No axis reads another axis or contributes to a holistic score.

children.title: Insight extraction
children.summary: Source findings become field-bound, cited evidence statements.

children.title: Insight identity reconciliation
children.summary: Groups statements of the same external fact without rewriting any statement.

children.title: Target relation and grounding
children.summary: Reports how evidence relates to a target and how well the target is supported.

children.title: Precedent
children.summary: Separates comparable coverage from favorable, mixed, or unfavorable outcome.

children.title: Measurement mapping
children.summary: Maps exact source-owned numeric passages against each target comparator contract.

nodes.title: Evidence review and calculation
nodes.summary: Explicit admission and evidence-unit deduplication precede descriptive statistics.
inputs: Mapped measurement candidates grouped by source record
nodes.guarantee: Only admitted, source-owned, unit-compatible, deduplicated scalars enter calculations.

nodes.title: Portable evidence result
nodes.summary: All traces, independent axes, review decisions, and source documents are packaged together.
outputs: Fields, landscape, safety, and evidence-map views
nodes.guarantee: Import, export, Assistant, and UI consume the same final contract without recalculation.

graphs.title: Screener
graphs.summary: Sorts one stage gate's question bank against a set of documents: what they answer, cited to the passage, and what they do not, alongside the discipline that owns it. Only the gate, the discipline and the question text decide anything. The bank also states whether each question is required at this gate or anticipatory, which is what separates a blocker from early warning.

nodes.title: Documents and gate
nodes.summary: A gate selects the question bank; the uploaded document types decide which of its questions can be assessed at all.
inputs: Optional attached context (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD), used for this run only
outputs: The material every question is read against

nodes.title: Applicability
nodes.summary: The one state config owns, and the question's own text is what states it. The shipped banks state no per-question restriction; each bank instead names the intervention classes it is written for, and a run for another modality is refused.
outputs: Questions the question text excludes from this run
Every other question, queued for assessment
nodes.guarantee: Which documents were uploaded is deliberately not an input. Withholding a question because of an assumption about where its answer lives would make a guess decide the result.

nodes.title: Document parsing
nodes.summary: Canonical documents become ordered, citable blocks. Attached context is read into text once, never chunked, and never stored.

nodes.title: Per-question decision
nodes.summary: One bounded call per question, each reading the same material. The questions are compound, so each is judged clause by clause: every part answered, some parts, or none.
inputs: Any attached context, as text, labelled
outputs: Partly answered, with what it still leaves open
Answered from a named context item
nodes.guarantee: Identical material on every call, so a citation is membership-checked and the expensive half of the prompt is a cacheable prefix rather than paid for once per question.

nodes.title: Portable gate review
nodes.summary: Every question the gate asks, each in one of four states, with the passages behind the answers and the source documents beside them.
outputs: The complete question list with states
nodes.guarantee: The denominator never shrinks and no count is stored, so the figures a reader sees are derived from the list they can open.

graphs.title: Chunker
graphs.summary: Normalizes DOCX and PPTX into one ordered block contract with stable citations and retained visuals.

nodes.title: Source file
nodes.summary: A supported document enters with its original filename stem as stable identity.
nodes.guarantee: Temporary upload names never enter citations.

nodes.title: Format-native parsing
nodes.summary: Each format preserves its native order, tables, metadata, and visuals.

children.title: DOCX parser
children.summary: Preserves body order, tables, and embedded images.

children.title: PPTX parser
children.summary: Retains slide text, tables, notes, positions, and rendered slide images.

nodes.title: Block normalization
nodes.summary: Format-native records converge to stable ContentBlocks and ImageAssets.
outputs: Ordered text, table, and image blocks
nodes.guarantee: Images remain canonical bytes rather than generated descriptions.

nodes.title: Section mapping
nodes.summary: A schema-bound stage labels every block once against the configured taxonomy.
nodes.guarantee: Unknown, duplicate, or omitted decisions fail the boundary.

nodes.title: Citable document
nodes.summary: Downstream tools receive one portable ordered block contract.
outputs: ContentBlock list with retained visual assets

graphs.title: Searcher
graphs.summary: Translates neutral retrieval intent into source-native requests while keeping credentials, rate limits, failures, and normalization inside adapters.

nodes.title: Retrieval intent
nodes.summary: Free text or typed source-neutral intents enter with requested source keys and the facets the caller can state.
inputs: Named subjects a source may address its API by
A publication-date bound, passed to sources that can apply it
nodes.guarantee: A stated condition anchors every field-addressed request; unstated, an adapter falls back to the intent's own scope rather than parsing the text.

nodes.title: Adapter planning
nodes.summary: Each registered source declares what evidence it owns, whose setting it describes, and what its output feeds, then owns its own grammar, applicability, credentials, and budget.
nodes.guarantee: Unknown source keys fail explicitly; ToolUniverse remains an injected connector, not a router. A source needing a named entity is ruled out with its reason rather than failing the run, and becomes plannable as soon as any caller states one. A source must declare both what it can be told and a downstream output it reaches, so a lane a reader can enable cannot be one nothing reads, and a dimension a caller can state cannot be one no lane can act on.

children.title: Applicability
children.summary: Checks declared evidence domains and entity requirements.

children.title: Request compilation
children.summary: Compacts intent concepts into valid native source grammar without dropping lineage.

children.title: Runtime policy
children.summary: Applies source-specific credentials, rate limits, concurrency, and request budgets.

nodes.title: Bounded scheduler
nodes.summary: Runnable source lanes execute concurrently and failures remain isolated.
nodes.guarantee: A slow or failed lane cannot corrupt another lane or occupy all runnable capacity.

nodes.title: Finding normalization
nodes.summary: Source responses converge to one finding contract, URL duplicates retain every path, and each finding keeps the class of evidence its lane owns.
outputs: Findings with evidence role and complete retrieval trace
nodes.guarantee: Reference-only records remain distinguishable from evidence-bearing passages, and findings are read in a mix of evidence classes rather than one class per model call, so a registry record and the literature it should be judged against reach the same prompt.

nodes.title: Search outcomes
nodes.summary: Direct callers receive URL-deduplicated findings together with one outcome per native request.
outputs: Normalized findings and isolated failure traces
Per-request lane report with the native query sent
nodes.guarantee: A lane that returned nothing, a lane that was skipped and a lane that failed stay distinguishable, so absence is never read as absence of evidence.

graphs.title: Assistant
graphs.summary: Answers read-only questions by navigating only the catalog, documentation, final results, source blocks, attachments, and cited URLs submitted in the current workspace.

nodes.title: Workspace bundle
nodes.summary: The client submits current catalog, eligible results, utility outputs, attachments, and conversation history.
nodes.guarantee: Active review drafts and provider credentials are never included.

nodes.title: Compact context maps
nodes.summary: Assistant starts with navigational summaries rather than placing every artifact into the prompt.
nodes.guarantee: Product documentation remains separate from product evidence.

nodes.title: Assistant skills
nodes.summary: Named procedures for reading two results together, or turning one into something sendable. An index of names is always present; a skill's steps are read only once chosen.
inputs: Which result types the workspace holds
outputs: A resident index, marking which can run
The full steps of the one chosen
nodes.guarantee: A skill whose results are absent is listed as unavailable rather than hidden, so a reader learns which run to make. Every claim a skill produces cites a finding on each side; none of them issues a verdict of its own or changes a result.

nodes.title: Bounded navigation loop
nodes.summary: The model chooses narrow read tools to gather only the context needed for the answer.
outputs: Targeted documentation, result, block, image, or cited-source reads
nodes.guarantee: Assistant cannot mutate analyses, run a tool pipeline, or start a new evidence search.

children.title: Product documentation
children.summary: Finds and reads canonical process, architecture, and terminology sections.

children.title: Result navigation
children.summary: Traverses eligible final analysis subtrees and direct utility output.

children.title: Document blocks
children.summary: Finds and pages exact parsed text or retained visuals packaged with results and attachments.

children.title: Cited URLs
children.summary: Opens only URLs already cited by a submitted analysis.

nodes.title: Grounded response
nodes.summary: The selected context and conversation produce one streamed read-only answer.
nodes.guarantee: An absent result remains explicit rather than being inferred from unrelated context.

nodes.title: Current conversation
nodes.summary: Floating and full-page views render the same in-memory conversation state.
nodes.guarantee: Conversation, results, blocks, and attachments reset together on reload.

graphs.title: Archivist
graphs.summary: Splits the work in two: a reviewed corpus is built from the archive offline, and a query over it is a filter with no model call at all.

nodes.title: Manifest and documents
nodes.summary: A folder of source documents plus a reviewed row per document declaring who wrote it, which document type it is, and which intervention class and indication it covers.
inputs: Source documents, not held in this repository
nodes.guarantee: A row is declared by a person only where a mistake would otherwise be invisible. Mislabelling a cTPP as an iTPP turns one candidate's commitment into a class-level ambition in every value below it, and no later check could notice; everything a document states in prose is extracted and checked against a quote instead. Every row is validated against the parsing configs and the shared vocabulary before any model call is made.

nodes.title: Attribute reading
nodes.summary: One call per document and attribute, over the parsed blocks. The model decides whether the document states the attribute, in which words, under which bound, and subject to which condition.
outputs: A value with its verbatim quote, or a recorded silence
nodes.guarantee: Each attribute is read on its own, and its prompt names the sibling attributes it must not absorb using the shared vocabulary's own words for them, so a shelf life cannot quietly become a storage temperature. The model never names a block, never types a number, and never resolves a tag: the block is found from the quote, so a quote and a citation cannot disagree. Silence is recorded as a row, which is what makes "none of twelve profiles specified this" answerable.

nodes.title: Verification and parsing
nodes.summary: Every offered value is checked against the document before it becomes a row, and any quantity in it is parsed in code.
outputs: Verified rows, or a flagged reading
nodes.guarantee: The value sits inside its quote, which sits inside the block it cites. The outer link rules out a fabricated sentence and the inner one rules out a paraphrase, which is the likelier error: a model asked for a shelf life will answer "about two years" from a document that wrote "24 months". Every check fails closed, so an unverifiable reading leaves no value and is flagged for review. A magnitude is read from the document's own words and never converted, and anything ambiguous parses as nothing.

nodes.title: Review and commit
nodes.summary: The corpus and a build report are written as committed artifacts, and a person reads them before anyone relies on a value.
inputs: Counts of what was discarded and why
nodes.guarantee: Static rather than built on demand, because every row is a model's reading of a confidential document and nobody should be shown a value cited to a block before a person has agreed with it. Rows are written in a stable order so a rebuild that changed one reading is a one-row diff. The report is separate from the corpus and carries what the corpus cannot: a discarded reading leaves no row, so only the report can say how many there were.

nodes.title: Filter and group
nodes.summary: A reader's filters select documents, and their rows are grouped by attribute and then by document type. No model call is involved.
outputs: Values, flagged readings, and silences, kept apart
nodes.guarantee: Values from different document types are never merged, because an iTPP states a class-level ambition and a cTPP states one candidate's commitment, and a number blending them describes neither product. For each attribute every matched document appears in exactly one of stated, uncertain, or silent, so a count is a count. Loading the corpus re-runs every invariant the build enforced, so a hand-edited quote cannot be served.

nodes.title: What the archive says
nodes.summary: Each value with the quote and block behind it, how many profiles specified the attribute, and which ones did not.
nodes.guarantee: No score, no ranking, and no reconciliation between two documents. This is the one workspace tool that judges nothing: its authority is the corpus, and a corpus is data rather than judgment, so what it returns is a selection of rows and counts a reader could recompute from them.
